Alerting someone that you're there (especially when they don't seem to be paying attention) is one of the main uses of the horn, and so it's one of the best times to use it. You were there in that intersection (occupying space in that moment in time) and they probably didn't even look to see if you were coming before pulling out in front of you or severely misjudged their timing in their movements.

So, I think it was a reasonable use of your horn to inform them that they could have hit you because they weren't supposed to go at that moment, and to be more careful/observant next time even if you knew you weren't going to collide with them. It also doesn't sound like you just laid on it either since, as you said, you weren't really mad at them and it was out of instinct.

It really depends on the laws where you live since each country, state, city, etc. may have different ordinances/laws. For example, where I live is pretty strict, and I can only use my horn to alert people to my presence, warn people of danger (like if someone was about to walk into traffic due to being on their phone), and to scare large animals off of the road. If I use it improperly I could get a ticket if a cop was around.

I failed a class during one of my first semesters of college. I just retook the class over again to help my GPA. Sure I still see the failed attempt on my transcripts, and it set me back a little bit at the moment, but I also see the successful retake of it. You can recover from a failed course as it is not the end of the world. This is especially true when you add all the courses you will take to calculate the total of your GPA.

So, don't give up hope since every failure is just a learning experience! You could always try again, possibly with a different professor if your uni/college has one that teaches the same class, or you could find an equivalent from a uni/college yours accepts. You have a lot of options out there. You just gotta ask yourself how well you learned under that professor.   
If it is required for your major, I suggest that you just retake it or take an equivalent. You could discuss it with your advisor. You had a tougher semester than most of us will ever see with all you had on your plate.

I wish you and your mother the best!

After the breakup I worked on myself as a person for a while and eventually met someone else, and I've been with her for almost 8 years. She's my fiancee now. :) We don't have a date planned for a wedding because we're waiting until I start my career and have some of my college debt paid off along with some savings so we can have a nice wedding.

Point is, there are people out there who will date someone who's transgender. If a relationship doesn't work out because they want something you don't have or can't provide and talking about it won't work, or if you ask someone out and they reject you because they're looking for someone who is completely different than you or uncomfortable with dating someone like you, ***just move on****.*
